newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's PHIBOR rates up on high C.Bank rate.
newsitem.headline: Manila's PHIBOR rates up on high C.Bank rate.

text.p: Philippine interbank offered rates (PHIBOR) jumped in all maturities on Thursday after the nine percentage-point increase in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 24 percent, traders said.
The rates, however, showed an inverted yield curve with the short-term tenors higher than the long-term.

Traders said this reflected continued cautiousness over the short-term effects of Thailand's de facto devaluation on Wednesday which forced the Philippine Central Bank to protect the peso and raise its rate.
As a result of the high short-term rates, non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) were heavily taking positions to move into fixed income investments, a bank official said.
"The volume of NDFs could swell to $500 million to $1 billion in the next few days if the Central Bank keeps its rate at 24 percent," he said.
